headline: The restart run still stands alone — days passing without a second touch. Strength's big session hasn't yet repeated either. Base holds, but rhythm remains unbuilt on both fronts.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture right now is one of two returning threads that haven't yet become fabric. The single Copenhagen restart run remains isolated — controlled and short, exactly what a re-entry should look like, but it needs company to count as a rhythm. Strength saw a genuinely large functional session break the two-week gap, yet that too still sits alone. The recent four-week running total looks inflated versus the prior block, but that number is carried almost entirely by the Åre ultra-volume, not by current frequency — a distinction worth holding onto so the mileage jump isn't misread as present momentum. Steps and background tracking are too sparse to say anything meaningful, and load metrics aren't reporting. The through-line: the Åre base is real and intact, but almost nothing in the last week has actively added to it beyond two isolated touches.
sections.trends: The year-to-date distance is dramatically ahead of the same point last year, which tells you the base built over the season is substantial and durable. But the shape of the last few weeks is irregular rather than building — a huge Åre block followed by a gap, then a cautious restart. That's a natural post-big-block trough, not regression, and it fits the year-round-readiness philosophy fine. What would make the shape coherent again is consistency returning: the base doesn't need defending, it needs re-engaging.
sections.threshold: The threshold read is now over two months old and unchanged because nothing has tested it. That staleness is the single clearest gap in the current picture — you have no fresh signal on where aerobic/threshold fitness actually sits after the ultra block and the layoff. The base almost certainly supports a strong number, but "almost certainly" is an assumption, not data. A sustained tempo effort would convert guesswork into a reading.
sections.zones: The restart run sat cleanly in low aerobic territory with a modest ceiling — appropriate for a re-entry, no notes. The last genuinely structured sessions before the layoff (late August) carried real Z3–Z4 time, so the capacity for intensity distribution is demonstrably there when the calendar allows it. The Åre runs were, by design, almost entirely Z1 time-on-feet. Nothing in the recent mix is misaligned; the issue is simply that there's too little recent running to speak of a distribution at all.
sections.hr_comparison: The returning functional session didn't carry HR, so there's no per-session shape to read from it. Historically the strength sessions sit in a controlled low-to-moderate band with occasional pushes into higher zones on the more intense days — consistent and unremarkable. Nothing in the current sensor-source picture warrants attention.
sections.calendar: The activity pattern remains clustered rather than spread — isolated touches with days of quiet between them, which is the same texture flagged over the past several days. The long running streak by week still holds, which is a testament to how the base was built, but the within-week density has thinned to near-single-session. That's the pattern most worth changing: not more volume, but more evenly distributed contact across the days.
sections.personal_bests: The 10K and Half bests fall right around this calendar week from last year, which is a useful reminder of what this athlete produces when sharpened — but chasing them isn't relevant right now with the threshold read stale and running frequency still re-establishing. They're a reference point, not a near-term target.

watch_items: Watch whether the restart run finally gains a second and third companion — the same open question as several days running, still unanswered.
Watch whether the big functional session repeats within the week rather than becoming another isolated touch.
Watch whether any tempo effort appears to finally refresh the now two-month-stale threshold read.
Watch whether sessions begin spreading across the week instead of clustering into isolated days.
